A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FLUID. Their complete main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable, and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original FLUID benchmark results, component ablations, throughput measurements, decoding trajectories and threshold sensitivity results.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds a noise-ratio ablation, an arithmetic decoding case study and adaptation-cost estimates.

M1.justification: Sections 4.1–4.4 and Algorithm 1 retain causal masking, the K-Head, two-stage training and confidence-gated inference. The more specific checkpoint name and clarified trainable-module wording do not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: The six evaluation benchmarks are unchanged, and the arithmetic case stays within existing reasoning coverage. However, v1 leaves its adaptation corpus unspecified, whereas v2 identifies instruction and conversation sources, including Chinese data. Whether actual training coverage changed cannot be determined.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same AR and diffusion comparators. The comparator configurations in Table 2 and the methods plotted in Figures 5–6 also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds a controlled Stage I noise-ratio sweep over 0%, 5%, 10% and 15%, explicitly holding other settings fixed. The proposed method's default remains 10%; existing training budgets, model scale, benchmark settings and threshold sweep are retained.

E4.justification: Section 5.4 adds the stochastic-restoration ablation, and Appendix C adds a token-entropy decoding case study. The earlier threshold study moves into Section 5.4 with its benchmark results retained, but its analysis of correlation strength across thresholds is removed.

E5.justification: Figure 6(b) retains Spearman ρ = -0.41 and p < 0.001 in both versions; v2 removes only their duplicate statement in Section 5.5. No repeated-run, seed or uncertainty-estimation practice changes are documented. The omitted threshold-specific correlations change result coverage.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and the threshold benchmark scores are unchanged. New Table 3 reports, for example, 91.0/60.8/59.8 at 0% noise on GSM8K/MATH500/HumanEval, alongside the retained 10% results. v2 also adds a K=15 to K=4 trajectory and an estimated 320 GPU-hour adaptation cost, while removing the threshold table's correlation column.

T1.justification: Equations 1–10 retain the same probability factorizations, corruption process, causal constraint, horizon definition and training objectives. No new formal assumptions, theorems, proofs or derivations are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central claims about efficient AR-to-diffusion adaptation, strictly causal alignment, elastic horizons and competitive performance. The added evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations linking moderate restoration noise to robustness and excessive noise to target distortion, and frames adaptation costs as comparable to parameter-efficient fine-tuning. It removes the threshold-specific alignment interpretation. The stated source-model and domain limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 5.1 newly documents response distillation from openPangu-Embedded-7B using Infinity-Instruct-7M, deepctrl-sft-data, moss-003-sft and UltraChat. Appendix D adds hardware and timing information: four 64GB GPUs, approximately 80 hours and 320 GPU-hours. The code-access destination changes from GitHub to Hugging Face. These substantially expand previously missing reproducibility information.

R1.justification: v2 adds four references supporting the newly documented training sources: Infinity Instruct, DeepCtrl, MOSS and UltraChat. The related-work discussion and positioning against earlier AR and diffusion methods remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds focused training-data and ablation paragraphs, moves the threshold discussion from Appendix C into Section 5.4, and introduces case-study and cost appendices. Most existing prose and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 3 and 5 and Figure 9. The old threshold Table 3 becomes main-text Table 4 without its correlation column. Existing displays undergo limited relocation, resizing and caption-placement changes; the original plotted results are retained.

improvement.justification: v1 omits adaptation-data provenance and hardware/time costs; v2 supplies these details and adds focused evidence for the existing noise setting and adaptive decoding behavior. These gains in transparency and supporting evidence outweigh the loss of threshold-specific correlations. The core method and main comparative evidence remain unchanged, limiting the overall improvement.
